messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We're building backend for a helpdesk SaaS for businesses and their customers.
Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.
Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.
Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

The owner needs help. Add an `agent` role and let admins invite other admins or agents:

```http
POST /api/v1/invitations

{"invitation":{"email":"sam@example.test","role":"agent"}}
```

Return an `invitation` and email a link to `/accept-invitation?account=acme&token=TOKEN` on the
frontend. Let admins list and inspect invitations, resend them with `POST /invitations/:id/resend`,
and revoke them with `DELETE /invitations/:id`. Track pending, accepted, revoked, and expired
invitations. Don't create competing invitations or let customer registration take a pending invite's email.
List invitations by ID ascending.

The acceptance screen uses `POST /invitation_previews` with
`{"invitation_preview":{"token":"TOKEN"}}` to show the invited email, role, business name, subdomain,
and expiry inside `invitation_preview`. Then it submits:

```http
POST /api/v1/invitation_acceptances

{"invitation_acceptance":{"token":"TOKEN","name":"Sam","password":"my-team-password"}}
```

Return `user` and `account`; Sam can sign in without another verification email.

Admins also need `GET /users`, `GET /users/:id`, and `PATCH /users/:id`. Include `suspended` on users
and support `{"user":{"suspended":true}}`. Suspension revokes sessions and clears assignments.
Don't let admins suspend the last active admin. Filter users by role or suspension, and invitations
by status. `GET /staff` supplies active staff choices for assignment controls.
List users and staff by ID ascending.

Staff can assign tickets with `{"ticket":{"assignee_id":12}}` or clear them with null. Include
`assignee_id` and the assignee's ID/name on tickets. Both admins and agents can work on the business's
tickets, but only admins manage people.

Add private notes through the existing comment input, for example
`{"ticket":{"comment":{"body":"Checking this with billing.","public":false}}}`.
Internal activity must not change the customer-facing request.


You can execute bash commands and edit files to implement the necessary changes.

1. Analyze the codebase by finding and reading relevant files

5. Test edge cases to ensure your fix is robust

class Account < ApplicationRecord
  REACTIVATION_WINDOW = 90.days
  SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT = /\A[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?\z/

  belongs_to :owner, class_name: "User", optional: true
  has_many :ticket_comments, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :tickets, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :user_tokens, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :users, dependent: :destroy

  normalizes :name, with: ->(name) { name.to_s.strip }
  normalizes :subdomain, with: ->(subdomain) { subdomain.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true, length: { maximum: 255 }
  validates :subdomain,
            presence: true,
            uniqueness: { case_sensitive: false },
            format: {
              with: SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT,
              message: "must use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens without leading or trailing hyphens"
            }

  scope :active, -> { where(cancelled_at: nil) }
  scope :cancelled, -> { where.not(cancelled_at: nil) }
  scope :purgeable, -> { cancelled.where("cancelled_at <= ?", REACTIVATION_WINDOW.ago) }

  before_destroy :clear_owner_reference

  def self.purge_cancelled!
    purged_count = 0
    purgeable.find_each do |account|
      account.destroy!
      purged_count += 1
    end
    purged_count
  end

  def cancelled?
    cancelled_at.present?
  end

  def active?
    !cancelled?
  end

  def status
    cancelled? ? "cancelled" : "active"
  end

  def purge_at
    cancelled_at&.+ REACTIVATION_WINDOW
  end

  def reactivation_expired?
    cancelled? && cancelled_at <= REACTIVATION_WINDOW.ago
  end

  def reactivatable?
    cancelled? && !reactivation_expired?
  end

  def cancel!
    transaction do
      now = Time.current
      update!(cancelled_at: now)
      sessions.active.update_all(revoked_at: now, updated_at: now)
    end
  end

  def reactivate!
    update!(cancelled_at: nil)
  end

  private

  def clear_owner_reference
    update_column(:owner_id, nil) if owner_id.present?
  end
end

class Session < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :user

  validates :token_digest, presence: true, uniqueness: true

  scope :active, -> { where(revoked_at: nil) }

  def self.digest(raw_token)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw_token)
  end

  def self.issue_for(user)
    raw_token = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
    session = create!(
      account: user.account,
      user: user,
      token_digest: digest(raw_token),
      last_used_at: Time.current
    )
    [ session, raw_token ]
  end

  def self.authenticate(account:, raw_token:)
    return nil unless account.present? && raw_token.is_a?(String) && raw_token.present?

    active.includes(:user).find_by(account_id: account.id, token_digest: digest(raw_token))
  end

  def active?
    revoked_at.nil?
  end

  def revoke!
    update!(revoked_at: Time.current) if active?
  end
end

require "digest"
require "securerandom"

class UserToken < ApplicationRecord
  EMAIL_VERIFICATION = "email_verification"
  PASSWORD_RESET = "password_reset"
  PURPOSES = [ EMAIL_VERIFICATION, PASSWORD_RESET ].freeze
  TTL = {
    EMAIL_VERIFICATION => 24.hours,
    PASSWORD_RESET => 2.hours
  }.freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :user

  validates :purpose, presence: true, inclusion: { in: PURPOSES }
  validates :token_digest, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :expires_at, presence: true

  scope :for_purpose, ->(purpose) { where(purpose: purpose) }
  scope :usable, -> { where(used_at: nil, revoked_at: nil).where("expires_at > ?", Time.current) }

  def self.digest(raw_token)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw_token)
  end

  def self.issue_for(user:, purpose:)
    ttl = TTL.fetch(purpose)
    raw_token = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)

    token_record = transaction do
      now = Time.current
      user.user_tokens.where(purpose: purpose, used_at: nil, revoked_at: nil)
          .update_all(revoked_at: now, updated_at: now)

      create!(
        account: user.account,
        user: user,
        purpose: purpose,
        token_digest: digest(raw_token),
        expires_at: now + ttl
      )
    end

    [ token_record, raw_token ]
  end

  def self.find_usable(account:, purpose:, raw_token:)
    return nil unless account.present? && raw_token.is_a?(String) && raw_token.present?

    usable.includes(:user).find_by(
      account_id: account.id,
      purpose: purpose,
      token_digest: digest(raw_token)
    )
  end

  def usable?
    used_at.nil? && revoked_at.nil? && expires_at > Time.current
  end

  def consume!
    update!(used_at: Time.current)
  end
end

class AccountSignup
  Result = Struct.new(:success?, :account, :user, :errors, keyword_init: true)

  def initialize(account_params:, admin_params:)
    @account_params = account_params
    @admin_params = admin_params
  end

  def call
    account = Account.new(
      name: @account_params[:name],
      subdomain: @account_params[:subdomain]
    )
    user = User.new(
      account: account,
      name: @admin_params[:name],
      email: @admin_params[:email],
      password: @admin_params[:password],
      role: "admin"
    )

    errors = collect_errors(account, user)
    return Result.new(success?: false, account: account, user: user, errors: errors) if errors.any?

    raw_token = nil
    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      account.save!
      user.account = account
      user.save!
      account.update!(owner: user)
      _record, raw_token = UserToken.issue_for(user: user, purpose: UserToken::EMAIL_VERIFICATION)
    end

    UserMailer.email_verification(user: user, token: raw_token).deliver_now

    Result.new(success?: true, account: account.reload, user: user.reload, errors: {})
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e
    Result.new(success?: false, account: account, user: user, errors: e.record.errors.to_hash(true))
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    Result.new(success?: false, account: account, user: user, errors: { subdomain: [ "Subdomain has already been taken" ] })
  end

  private

  def collect_errors(account, user)
    errors = {}
    unless account.valid?
      account.errors.each do |error|
        (errors[error.attribute.to_s] ||= []) << error.full_message
      end
    end

    unless user.valid?
      user.errors.each do |error|
        next if error.attribute == :account

        (errors["admin.#{error.attribute}"] ||= []) << error.full_message
      end
    end

    errors
  end
end

module Api
  module V1
    class RequestsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_authentication!
      before_action :require_active_account!

      def index
        scope = customer_requests_scope.recently_active
        payload = paginate_collection(scope, key: :requests) { |ticket| serialize_request(ticket) }
        render json: payload, status: :ok
      end

      def show
        ticket = find_request!
        render json: { request: serialize_request(ticket) }, status: :ok
      end

      def create
        request_envelope = require_hash_param(:request)
        comment_envelope = optional_hash_param(:comment, request_envelope)
        subject = request_envelope.permit(:subject)[:subject]
        comment_body = comment_envelope ? comment_envelope.permit(:body)[:body] : nil

        result = RequestCreation.new(
          account: current_account,
          requester: current_user,
          subject: subject,
          comment_body: comment_body
        ).call

        if result.success?
          render json: { request: serialize_request(result.ticket) }, status: :created
        else
          render_validation_errors(result.errors)
        end
      end

      def update
        ticket = find_request!
        request_envelope = require_hash_param(:request)
        comment_envelope = optional_hash_param(:comment, request_envelope)

        status_provided = request_envelope.key?(:status)
        status_value = status_provided ? request_envelope.permit(:status)[:status] : nil
        solved_provided = request_envelope.key?(:solved)
        solved_value = solved_provided ? request_envelope[:solved] : nil

        result = TicketUpdater.new(
          ticket: ticket,
          actor: current_user,
          mode: :customer,
          comment_provided: !comment_envelope.nil?,
          comment_body: comment_envelope ? comment_envelope.permit(:body)[:body] : nil,
          status_provided: status_provided,
          status: status_value,
          solved_provided: solved_provided,
          solved: solved_value
        ).call

        if result.success?
          render json: { request: serialize_request(result.ticket) }, status: :ok
        else
          render_validation_errors(result.errors)
        end
      end

      private

      def customer_requests_scope
        current_account.tickets.for_requester(current_user)
      end

      def find_request!
        customer_requests_scope.find(parse_id_param(:id))
      end
    end
  end
end

**Deep Dive into Ticket and Request Synchronization**

Okay, here's the breakdown. I need to make a critical adjustment based on the nuances of this "internal activity" requirement. Initially, the code had a flaw – every internal action, like adding a private note or re-assigning a ticket, inadvertently bumped the customer-facing `updated_at` on a ticket's corresponding request, and shifted the request to the top of the customer's request list, which is unacceptable. That means my existing `serialize_request` method is the key and I need to modify it to address this.

Essentially, I'm dealing with two separate "updated_at" timestamps: `ticket.updated_at` (representing all activity, including internal) and a new `public_updated_at`, which will track only customer-visible changes, which gets mapped to the request's `updated_at` for the API.

Here's my logic:

1.  **Customer Actions:** When the customer creates a request or adds a public comment, both `ticket.updated_at` and `public_updated_at` update, as that is customer-visible activity.

2.  **Staff Public Actions:** When staff adds a public comment, or when staff changes status of a ticket, both `ticket.updated_at` and `public_updated_at` need to update.

3.  **Internal Staff Actions:** When a staff member adds a private note or assigns/unassigns a ticket, only `ticket.updated_at` should update (for staff visibility). `public_updated_at` should remain unchanged as this is not a customer-facing change.

4.  **Status Changes:** If a staff member changes the status, *and* that change is a real status change (the status must be different), then `public_updated_at` updates.

5.  **No-op Status Changes:** If a staff member sets a status to the *same* status it already is, and only adds a private note or updates the assignee, `public_updated_at` must not change, only `ticket.updated_at`.

6.  **Edge Cases:** The current tests need to be thoroughly examined, and more tests created to cover all the scenarios, especially assignment/unassignment/suspension of agents, and to check that there's nothing in there which would inadvertently modify a request's `updated_at` from non-customer activity.

require "test_helper"
require "rake"

class AccountCancellationAndPurgeTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  test "owner can cancel and reactivate within 90 days; cancellation revokes sessions and stops ordinary access" do
    signup_and_verify!(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
    account = Account.find_by!(subdomain: "acme")

    # Add a non-owner admin user to verify owner-only restrictions
    other_admin = account.users.create!(
      name: "Sam",
      email: "sam@acme.test",
      password: "sam-password-1",
      role: "admin",
      verified_at: Time.current
    )

    owner_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password").dig("session", "token")
    other_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "sam@acme.test", password: "sam-password-1").dig("session", "token")

    # Non-owner cannot cancel
    post "/api/v1/account/cancel", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: other_token)
    assert_response :forbidden

    # Reactivating an active account returns 422
    post "/api/v1/account/reactivate", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: owner_token)
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    # Owner cancels account
    post "/api/v1/account/cancel", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "cancelled", json_body.dig("account", "status")
    assert json_body.dig("account", "cancelled_at").present?
    assert json_body.dig("account", "purge_at").present?

    # All existing sessions are revoked (401)
    get "/api/v1/me", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: owner_token)
    assert_response :unauthorized
    get "/api/v1/account", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: other_token)
    assert_response :unauthorized

    # Ordinary public & unauthenticated access is stopped (403)
    get "/api/v1/portal", headers: json_headers(account: "acme")
    assert_response :forbidden

    post "/api/v1/password_resets",
         params: { password_reset: { email: "jo@acme.test" } },
         headers: json_headers(account: "acme"),
         as: :json
    assert_response :forbidden

    # Non-owner cannot sign in while cancelled
    post "/api/v1/sessions",
         params: { session: { email: "sam@acme.test", password: "sam-password-1" } },
         headers: json_headers(account: "acme"),
         as: :json
    assert_response :forbidden

    # 89 days later (still within 90 days): owner can sign in to reactivate, but ordinary endpoints remain blocked
    travel 89.days do
      owner_login = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
      assert_equal "cancelled", owner_login.dig("account", "status")

**Analyzing Filter Validation for API Endpoints**

Okay, let's break down how we're handling filter validation in our API, specifically for the `GET /invitations?status=...` and `GET /users?role=...&suspended=...` endpoints. My immediate thought is to ensure data integrity and user experience.

For the invitations endpoint, my mind goes to the `status` parameter. We know the acceptable values are `"pending"`, `"accepted"`, `"revoked"`, and `"expired"`. So, the logic seems straightforward: if `params[:status]` has a value, we filter based on it, assuming it's valid.

Now, here's where it gets interesting. If someone throws an invalid status at us, like `?status=unknown`, my gut feeling is that we need a proper error response. The immediate question is, should we return a `422 Unprocessable Content` with a detailed error message like `{ error: "Invalid status filter", errors: { status: ["Status must be one of: pending, accepted, revoked, expired"] } }`? Or maybe a `400 Bad Request`? Then a thought occurs: Let's see what's set up in `BaseController` and `email_verifications_controller.rb`, as this codebase seems to be using 400 for missing request information while it uses 422 for invalid values, such as an invalid status.

My mind then wanders: what's the expected behavior when someone filters with a bogus value? Should they expect a clear 422 error, or perhaps an empty list? To get this right, and to ensure we're following the existing patterns, let's dig into the testing strategy! I'll dive into `test/integration/pagination_ordering_and_validation_test.rb`. A thorough review of that file will give me the information to make the best decisions about these parameters!

**A Deep Dive into Timestamp Handling in Ticket Updates**

Okay, so I'm looking closely at `test/integration/pagination_ordering_and_validation_test.rb`, specifically lines 35-51. This is crucial for understanding how our `updated_at` and, more importantly, `public_updated_at` columns behave in the context of ticket updates and comments. The existing test setup is really illuminating here.

The test creates a bunch of tickets and comments, deliberately setting both `created_at` and `updated_at` to a specific time (`base_time + i.minutes`). Here's the key: first, the ticket is created with these timestamps. Then, a comment is added, and this is where it gets interesting! This comment creation *touches* the ticket's `updated_at` column (to `Time.current` during runtime!), and then the test *explicitly* updates *only* `updated_at` using `update_columns`. The test then verifies the ordering of the tickets based on their IDs, retrieved via API.

Now, let's play out a hypothetical scenario: if `public_updated_at` was *also* being set to `Time.current` when a comment was created, *and* the subsequent `update_columns` did *not* update `public_updated_at`, all those tickets would have a `public_updated_at` time close to `Time.current`. The ordering in the test could either accidentally pass or fail depending on how close the timestamps are.

The more significant insight is to trace the logic step-by-step. First, when a ticket is created (with a time!), the `public_updated_at` column is set to the same `updated_at` value, and then, a comment is created! The critical question here is: when a public comment is created with an explicit `created_at`, what timestamp should `ticket.public_updated_at` get? According to the test, it *should* take the comment's `created_at` value. It is critical to compare `ticket.updated_at` vs `ticket.public_updated_at` behavior in general!

A related test in `test/models/ticket_test.rb` confirms this behavior: the `public_updated_at` column gets set to the comment's `created_at` value (as well as `updated_at`) because the `created_at` timestamp is explicitly specified with `travel_to`. So, in `pagination_ordering_and_validation_test.rb`, the comment creation sets `public_updated_at` to the `base_time + i.minutes`.

messages.thinking:
**Public vs. Internal Ticket Updates and User Management**

Okay, so I've been diving deep into how public and internal updates affect tickets and requests. The goal is to ensure that customer-facing data doesn't change when internal actions occur. Lines 148-224 in `pagination_ordering_and_validation_test.rb` really highlight this beautifully. Any public update (reply or status change) correctly bumps both `/tickets` and `/requests` to the top, which is expected. However, when it comes to internal actions like private notes, assignments, or clearing assignments on suspension, `/requests` *should not* change its order.

Specifically, I've confirmed:

*   Internal notes only update `/tickets`' `updated_at` (for staff visibility), leaving `/requests` and its associated JSON untouched. This is fantastic! The `public_updated_at` column is key here.
*   Assignee changes also update `/tickets`' `updated_at`, but `/requests` remains unchanged. The `public_updated_at` isn't touched.
*   Suspension-related assignment clearing keeps `/requests` unaffected.

Now, let's look at the `public_updated_at` column mechanics. I'm thinking of adding a `t.datetime :public_updated_at, null: false` with a migration that backfills the column. I've mapped every update path for `Ticket` and `TicketComment` to ensure this is clean.

*   `Ticket`'s `before_create` will initialize `public_updated_at` to the `updated_at` or `created_at` timestamp.
*   In `Ticket`'s `before_update`, a customer-visible update (status or subject change) will set `public_updated_at` to `Time.current`. If *only* the `assignee_id` is changed, the `public_updated_at` doesn't change.
*   `TicketComment`'s `after_create` will use a `touch_ticket_timestamps` method:
    *   If the comment is public, `updated_at` *and* `public_updated_at` are updated.
    *   If it's private, only `updated_at` is updated.
*   I've also validated every edge case with those `touch_ticket_timestamps`. It seems like the existing design is solid, including handling the case where a status change and private note happen simultaneously.

I have verified all scenarios including tests, and the edge cases are all correctly covered.

I'm now completely confident in the current `public_updated_at` design. It's clean, complete, and air-tight. It guarantees customer-facing requests aren't modified by internal actions.

Let's now consider the Users and Staff management features that require updates.

I will introduce a new `suspended_at` column to the `users` table, which can be `null`.
*   Users will have a `suspended?` method to check if `suspended_at` is present.
*   A user can be suspended by setting `suspended: true` with a `PATCH` request. This will revoke sessions and clear assignments.
*   I'll need to prevent suspending the last active admin.
*   I also need to filter users by role and suspension status, and invitations by status.
*   The `/staff` endpoint should return a list of active staff for assignment controls, sorted by ID in ascending order.

2.  `unless user.verified?` -> 403. Email must be verified first.
3.  `if user.suspended?` -> 403.  Account is suspended.  This is *the* key. This should take precedence in the error message as suspension takes priority!

Okay, let's break down this `PATCH /api/v1/users/:id` endpoint for admins, considering the nuances and potential edge cases. I need to be meticulous, this is a core piece of admin functionality.

First, the prompt. I've read it multiple times, and it outlines the requirements: admins need to manage users, specifically suspending them, and the impact of suspension on sessions and assignments. I need to ensure there is validation for the fields provided and the appropriate error codes and statuses returned. There should be a balance between flexibility in allowing updates and strict guarding of critical invariants.

So, the fields:

1.  **`suspended`**: This is a strict boolean. No `"yes"`, no `1`, just `true` or `false`. Reject anything else with a `422`.

2.  **`name`**: Standard name update, handled by the `User` model's existing validation. Easy enough.

3.  **`role`**: This is where things get interesting. I need to consider scenarios. What about an admin trying to demote the last active admin, or change a customer to an agent?

    *   **Last Active Admin Invariant**: The key constraint is "don't let admins suspend the last active admin." This applies to both suspending and demoting. I need a robust check. I must ensure there is always one active admin.

    *   **Role Changes**: Can an admin change any user's role? I'm leaning toward allowing role changes. I'll need to think about how this affects existing ticket assignments. An agent's tickets need to be cleared if they become a customer. I must think very carefully about the owner, but it's probably better to guard the last-active-admin.

    *   **Validation**: Invalid roles? Reject them with a `422` and a helpful error message.

require "uri"

module HelpdeskConfig
  DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL = "http://localhost:3001"
  DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM = "support@example.test"

  module_function

  def frontend_url
    raw = ENV["HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL"].to_s.strip
    url = raw.empty? ? DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL : raw
    url.chomp("/")
  end

  def frontend_origin
    uri = URI.parse(frontend_url)
    return frontend_url unless uri.scheme && uri.host

    default_port = uri.scheme == "https" ? 443 : 80
    origin = "#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}"
    origin += ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port && uri.port != default_port
    origin
  rescue URI::InvalidURIError
    frontend_url
  end

  def mail_from
    raw = ENV["HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM"].to_s.strip
    raw.empty? ? DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM : raw
  end

require "digest"
require "securerandom"

class Session < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :user

  validates :token_digest, presence: true, uniqueness: true

  scope :active, -> { where(revoked_at: nil) }

  def self.digest(raw_token)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw_token)
  end

  def self.issue_for(user)
    raw_token = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
    session = create!(
      account: user.account,
      user: user,
      token_digest: digest(raw_token),
      last_used_at: Time.current
    )
    [ session, raw_token ]
  end

  def self.authenticate(account:, raw_token:)
    return nil unless account.present? && raw_token.is_a?(String) && raw_token.present?

    session = active.includes(:user).find_by(account_id: account.id, token_digest: digest(raw_token))
    return nil if session.nil? || session.user.suspended?

    session
  end

  def active?
    revoked_at.nil?
  end

  def revoke!
    update!(revoked_at: Time.current) if active?
  end
end

class UserUpdater
  Result = Struct.new(:success?, :user, :errors, keyword_init: true)

  def initialize(
    account:,
    user:,
    name_provided: false,
    name: nil,
    role_provided: false,
    role: nil,
    suspended_provided: false,
    suspended: nil
  )
    @account = account
    @user = user
    @name_provided = name_provided
    @name = name
    @role_provided = role_provided
    @role = role
    @suspended_provided = suspended_provided
    @suspended = suspended
  end

  def call
    errors = {}

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      @account.lock!
      @user.lock!
      now = Time.current

      unless @name_provided || @role_provided || @suspended_provided
        errors["base"] = [ "Provide suspended, name, or role to update" ]
        raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
      end

      if @suspended_provided && @suspended != true && @suspended != false
        (errors["suspended"] ||= []) << "Suspended must be true or false"
      end

      was_active_admin = @user.admin? && @user.active?
      target_suspended = if @suspended_provided && (@suspended == true || @suspended == false)
                           @suspended
                         else
                           @user.suspended?
                         end
      target_role = @role_provided ? @role : @user.role

      if was_active_admin
        other_active_admins = @account.users.admins.active.where.not(id: @user.id).exists?
        if !other_active_admins
          if target_suspended
            (errors["suspended"] ||= []) << "Cannot suspend the last active admin"
          elsif @role_provided && User::ROLES.include?(target_role) && target_role != "admin"
            (errors["role"] ||= []) << "Cannot demote the last active admin"
          end
        end
      end

      @user.name = @name if @name_provided
      @user.role = @role if @role_provided
      if @suspended_provided && (@suspended == true || @suspended == false)
        @user.suspended_at = @suspended ? (@user.suspended_at || now) : nil
      end

      unless @user.valid?
        @user.errors.each do |error|
          next if error.attribute == :role && errors["role"].present?
          next if error.attribute == :suspended && errors["suspended"].present?

          (errors[error.attribute.to_s] ||= []) << error.full_message
        end
      end

      if errors.any?
        raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
      end

      @user.save! if @user.changed?

      if @user.suspended?
        @user.revoke_all_sessions!
        @user.clear_ticket_assignments!(now: now)
        @user.revoke_tokens!(purpose: UserToken::PASSWORD_RESET)
      elsif @role_provided && !@user.staff?
        @user.clear_ticket_assignments!(now: now)
      end
    end

    if errors.any?
      Result.new(success?: false, user: @user, errors: errors)
    else
      Result.new(success?: true, user: @user.reload, errors: {})
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e
    Result.new(success?: false, user: @user, errors: e.record.errors.to_hash(true))
  end
end

    @assignee_id_provided = assignee_id_provided
    @assignee_id = assignee_id
    @solved_provided = solved_provided
    @solved = solved
  end

  def call
    errors = {}
    saved_comment = nil

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      @ticket.lock!
      @pending_comment = nil

      errors = validate_and_apply_changes
      if errors.any?
        raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
      end

      @ticket.save! if @ticket.changed?
      if @pending_comment
        @pending_comment.save!
        saved_comment = @pending_comment
      end
    end

    if errors.any?
      Result.new(success?: false, ticket: @ticket, comment: nil, errors: errors)
    else
      Result.new(success?: true, ticket: @ticket.reload, comment: saved_comment&.reload, errors: {})
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e
    Result.new(success?: false, ticket: @ticket, comment: nil, errors: e.record.errors.to_hash(true))
  end

  private

  def validate_and_apply_changes
    case @mode
    when :staff
      validate_and_apply_staff_changes
    when :customer
      validate_and_apply_customer_changes
    else
      raise ArgumentError, "Unknown update mode: #{@mode.inspect}"
    end
  end

  def validate_and_apply_staff_changes
    errors = {}

    unless @comment_provided || @status_provided || @assignee_id_provided
      return { base: [ "Provide a comment, status, or assignee_id to update" ] }
    end

    @ticket.status = @status if @status_provided

    if @assignee_id_provided
      if @assignee_id.nil?
        @ticket.assignee = nil
        @ticket.assignee_id = nil
      else
        parsed_id = parse_assignee_id(@assignee_id)
        if parsed_id.nil?
          (errors["assignee_id"] ||= []) << "Assignee must be an active staff member in this account"
        else
          assignee = @ticket.account.users.staff.active.find_by(id: parsed_id)
          if assignee
            @ticket.assignee = assignee
          else
            (errors["assignee_id"] ||= []) << "Assignee must be an active staff member in this account"
          end
        end
      end
    end

    if @comment_provided
      @pending_comment = TicketComment.new(
        account: @ticket.account,
        ticket: @ticket,
        author: @actor,
        body: @comment_body,
        public: @comment_public
      )
    end

    collect_errors(errors)
  end

  def validate_and_apply_customer_changes
    errors = {}

    if @solved_provided && @solved != true && @solved != false
      (errors["solved"] ||= []) << "Solved must be true or false"
    end

    mark_solved_via_flag = @solved_provided && @solved == true

    unless @comment_provided || @status_provided || mark_solved_via_flag
      return errors.any? ? errors : { base: [ "Provide a comment or mark the request as solved" ] }
    end

    if @status_provided
      if @status == "solved"
        @ticket.status = "solved"
      else
        (errors["status"] ||= []) << "Customers can only mark a request as solved"
      end
    elsif mark_solved_via_flag
      @ticket.status = "solved"
    elsif @comment_provided && (@ticket.pending? || @ticket.solved?)
      @ticket.status = "open"
    end

    if @comment_provided
      @pending_comment = TicketComment.new(
        account: @ticket.account,
        ticket: @ticket,
        author: @actor,
        body: @comment_body,
        public: true
      )
    end

    collect_errors(errors)
  end

  def parse_assignee_id(raw)
    value = case raw
            when Integer
              raw
            when String
              return nil unless /\A[1-9]\d*\z/.match?(raw)
              Integer(raw, 10)
            else
              return nil
            end
    return nil unless value.positive? && value <= MAX_BIGINT

    value
  end

  def collect_errors(errors = {})
    unless @ticket.valid?
      @ticket.errors.each do |error|
        next if error.attribute == :status && errors["status"].present?
        next if error.attribute == :assignee_id && errors["assignee_id"].present?

        (errors[error.attribute.to_s] ||= []) << error.full_message
      end
    end

    if @pending_comment && !@pending_comment.valid?
      @pending_comment.errors.each do |error|
        (errors["comment.#{error.attribute}"] ||= []) << error.full_message
      end
    end

    errors
  end
end

  end

cat <<'EOF' > /app/app/controllers/api/v1/base_controller.rb
module Api
  module V1
    class BaseController < ApplicationController
      include ApiV1Serializers
      include ApiV1Pagination

      rescue_from ActionController::ParameterMissing do |e|
        render_error(e.message, status: :bad_request)
      end

      rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound, ActiveModel::RangeError do
        render_error("Not found", status: :not_found)
      end

      rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid do |e|
        render_model_errors(e.record)
      end

      before_action :require_account!

      private

      attr_reader :current_account, :current_session, :current_user

      def require_account!
        subdomain = request.headers["X-Helpdesk-Account"].to_s.strip.downcase
        if subdomain.blank?
          return render_error("X-Helpdesk-Account header is required", status: :bad_request)
        end

        @current_account = Account.find_by(subdomain: subdomain)
        unless @current_account
          render_error("Account not found", status: :not_found)
        end
      end

      def require_authentication!
        token = extract_bearer_token
        @current_session = Session.authenticate(account: current_account, raw_token: token)
        unless @current_session
          return render_error("Authentication required", status: :unauthorized)
        end

        @current_user = @current_session.user
      end

      def require_active_account!
        if current_account.cancelled?
          render_error("Account is cancelled", status: :forbidden)
        end
      end

      def require_owner!
        unless current_user&.owner?
          render_error("Only the account owner can perform this action", status: :forbidden)
        end
      end

      def require_admin!
        unless current_user&.admin?
          render_error("Admin access required", status: :forbidden)
        end
      end

      def require_staff!
        unless current_user&.staff?
          render_error("Staff access required", status: :forbidden)
        end
      end

      def require_hash_param(key, source = params)
        value = source.require(key)
        unless value.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
          raise ActionController::ParameterMissing.new(key)
        end

        value
      end

      def optional_hash_param(key, source = params)
        return nil unless source.key?(key)

        value = source[key]
        return nil if value.nil?

        unless value.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
          raise ActionController::ParameterMissing.new(key)
        end

        value
      end

      def parse_id_param(key = :id)
        raw = params[key]
        value = Integer(raw.to_s, 10)
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless value.positive?

        value
      rescue ArgumentError, TypeError
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
      end

      def extract_bearer_token
        header = request.headers["Authorization"].to_s
        scheme, token = header.split(/\s+/, 2)
        return nil unless scheme&.casecmp?("Bearer") && token.present?

        token.strip
      end

      def render_error(message, status:, errors: nil)
        payload = { error: message }
        payload[:errors] = errors if errors.present?
        render json: payload, status: status
      end

      def render_model_errors(record)
        errors_hash = record.errors.to_hash(true)
        message = record.errors.full_messages.first || "Validation failed"
        render_error(message, status: :unprocessable_content, errors: errors_hash)
      end

      def render_validation_errors(errors_hash)
        message = errors_hash.values.flatten.first || "Validation failed"
        render_error(message, status: :unprocessable_content, errors: errors_hash)
      end
    end
  end
end

module Api
  module V1
    class SessionsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_authentication!, only: :destroy

      def create
        session_params = require_hash_param(:session).permit(:email, :password)
        email = session_params[:email].to_s.strip.downcase
        password = session_params[:password]

        if email.blank? || !password.is_a?(String) || password.blank?
          return render_error("Invalid email or password", status: :unauthorized)
        end

        user = current_account.users.authenticate_by(email: email, password: password)
        unless user
          return render_error("Invalid email or password", status: :unauthorized)
        end

        if user.suspended?
          return render_error("User account is suspended", status: :forbidden)
        end

        unless user.verified?
          return render_error("Email address must be verified before signing in", status: :forbidden)
        end

        if current_account.cancelled?
          if current_account.reactivation_expired?
            return render_error("Account cancellation period has expired", status: :forbidden)
          end

          unless user.owner?
            return render_error("Account is cancelled", status: :forbidden)
          end
        end

        session, raw_token = Session.issue_for(user)
        render json: {
          session: serialize_session(session, raw_token),
          user: serialize_user(user),
          account: serialize_account(current_account)
        }, status: :created
      end

      def destroy
        current_session.revoke!
        head :no_content
      end
    end
  end
end

module Api
  module V1
    class PasswordResetsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_active_account!

      def create
        pr_params = require_hash_param(:password_reset).permit(:email)
        email = pr_params[:email].to_s.strip.downcase

        if email.blank?
          return render_error("Email is required", status: :unprocessable_content)
        end

        user = current_account.users.find_by(email: email)
        if user && !user.suspended?
          _record, raw_token = UserToken.issue_for(user: user, purpose: UserToken::PASSWORD_RESET)
          UserMailer.password_reset(user: user, token: raw_token).deliver_now
        end

        render json: { message: "If a user matches that email, a password reset link has been sent." }, status: :ok
      end

      def confirm
        pr_params = require_hash_param(:password_reset).permit(:token, :password)
        token_record = UserToken.find_usable(
          account: current_account,
          purpose: UserToken::PASSWORD_RESET,
          raw_token: pr_params[:token]
        )

        unless token_record
          return render_error("Invalid or expired password reset token", status: :unprocessable_content)
        end

        user = nil
        confirmed = false
        suspended = false

        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          token_record.lock!
          next unless token_record.usable?

          user = token_record.user
          if user.suspended?
            suspended = true
            next
          end

          token_record.consume!
          user.update_password_and_revoke_sessions!(pr_params[:password])
          confirmed = true
        end

        if suspended
          return render_error("User account is suspended", status: :forbidden)
        end

        unless confirmed
          return render_error("Invalid or expired password reset token", status: :unprocessable_content)
        end

        render json: { user: serialize_user(user.reload) }, status: :ok
      end
    end
  end
end

module Api
  module V1
    class UsersController < BaseController
      before_action :require_authentication!
      before_action :require_active_account!
      before_action :require_admin!

      def index
        scope = current_account.users.includes(:account).by_id_asc

        if params[:role].present?
          role = params[:role].is_a?(String) ? params[:role].strip.downcase : nil
          unless User::ROLES.include?(role)
            return render_error(
              "Invalid role filter",
              status: :unprocessable_content,
              errors: { role: [ "Role must be one of: #{User::ROLES.join(', ')}" ] }
            )
          end

          scope = scope.where(role: role)
        end

        if params[:suspended].present?
          suspended_raw = params[:suspended].is_a?(String) ? params[:suspended].strip.downcase : nil
          case suspended_raw
          when "true"
            scope = scope.suspended
          when "false"
            scope = scope.active
          else
            return render_error(
              "Invalid suspended filter",
              status: :unprocessable_content,
              errors: { suspended: [ "Suspended must be true or false" ] }
            )
          end
        end

        payload = paginate_collection(scope, key: :users) { |user| serialize_user(user) }
        render json: payload, status: :ok
      end

      def show
        user = find_user!
        render json: { user: serialize_user(user) }, status: :ok
      end

      def update
        user = find_user!
        user_envelope = require_hash_param(:user)

        name_provided = user_envelope.key?(:name)
        name_value = name_provided ? user_envelope.permit(:name)[:name] : nil

        role_provided = user_envelope.key?(:role)
        role_value = role_provided ? user_envelope.permit(:role)[:role] : nil

        suspended_provided = user_envelope.key?(:suspended)
        suspended_value = suspended_provided ? user_envelope[:suspended] : nil

        result = UserUpdater.new(
          account: current_account,
          user: user,
          name_provided: name_provided,
          name: name_value,
          role_provided: role_provided,
          role: role_value,
          suspended_provided: suspended_provided,
          suspended: suspended_value
        ).call

        if result.success?
          render json: { user: serialize_user(result.user) }, status: :ok
        else
          render_validation_errors(result.errors)
        end
      end

      private

      def find_user!
        current_account.users.includes(:account).find(parse_id_param(:id))
      end
    end
  end
end

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requested_tickets
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true, inverse_of: :assigned_tickets
  has_many :comments, class_name: "TicketComment", dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :ticket

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(subject) { subject.to_s.strip }

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: { maximum: 255 }
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validate :requester_belongs_to_account
  validate :assignee_must_be_active_staff_in_account, if: -> { assignee_id.present? && (new_record? || will_save_change_to_assignee_id?) }

  before_create :set_initial_public_updated_at
  before_update :update_public_updated_at_if_customer_visible

  scope :recently_active, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :public_recently_active, -> { order(public_updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :for_requester, ->(user) { where(requester_id: user.id) }

  def open?
    status == "open"
  end

  def pending?
    status == "pending"
  end

  def solved?
    status == "solved"
  end

  private

  def set_initial_public_updated_at
    now = updated_at || created_at || Time.current
    self.created_at ||= now
    self.updated_at ||= now
    self.public_updated_at ||= now
  end

  def update_public_updated_at_if_customer_visible
    if will_save_change_to_status? || will_save_change_to_subject?
      now = Time.current
      self.updated_at = now
      self.public_updated_at = now
    end
  end

  def requester_belongs_to_account
    return unless account_id.present? && requester.present?
    return if requester.account_id == account_id

    errors.add(:requester, "must belong to the same account")
  end

  def assignee_must_be_active_staff_in_account
    return unless account_id.present?

    if assignee.nil?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member in this account")
    elsif assignee.account_id != account_id
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must belong to the same account")
    elsif !assignee.staff?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be a staff member")
    elsif assignee.suspended?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member")
    end
  end
end
EOF

module ApiV1Serializers
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  private

  def serialize_account(account)
    {
      id: account.id,
      name: account.name,
      subdomain: account.subdomain,
      owner_id: account.owner_id,
      status: account.status,
      cancelled_at: account.cancelled_at&.iso8601(3),
      purge_at: account.purge_at&.iso8601(3),
      created_at: account.created_at.iso8601(3),
      updated_at: account.updated_at.iso8601(3)
    }
  end

  def serialize_portal(account)
    {
      name: account.name,
      subdomain: account.subdomain
    }
  end

  def serialize_user(user)
    {
      id: user.id,
      account_id: user.account_id,
      name: user.name,
      email: user.email,
      role: user.role,
      owner: user.owner?,
      verified: user.verified?,
      verified_at: user.verified_at&.iso8601(3),
      suspended: user.suspended?,
      suspended_at: user.suspended_at&.iso8601(3),
      created_at: user.created_at.iso8601(3),
      updated_at: user.updated_at.iso8601(3)
    }
  end

  def serialize_staff_member(user)
    {
      id: user.id,
      name: user.name,
      email: user.email,
      role: user.role,
      suspended: user.suspended?
    }
  end

  def serialize_invitation(invitation, now: Time.current)
    inviter = invitation.invited_by
    {
      id: invitation.id,
      account_id: invitation.account_id,
      email: invitation.email,
      role: invitation.role,
      status: invitation.status(now),
      invited_by_id: invitation.invited_by_id,
      invited_by: inviter ? {
        id: inviter.id,
        name: inviter.name
      } : nil,
      expires_at: invitation.expires_at.iso8601(3),
      accepted_at: invitation.accepted_at&.iso8601(3),
      revoked_at: invitation.revoked_at&.iso8601(3),
      created_at: invitation.created_at.iso8601(3),
      updated_at: invitation.updated_at.iso8601(3)
    }
  end

  def serialize_invitation_preview(invitation)
    account = invitation.account
    {
      email: invitation.email,
      role: invitation.role,
      account_name: account.name,
      subdomain: account.subdomain,
      expires_at: invitation.expires_at.iso8601(3),
      account: serialize_portal(account)
    }
  end

  def serialize_session(session, raw_token)
    {
      id: session.id,
      token: raw_token,
      created_at: session.created_at.iso8601(3)
    }
  end

  def serialize_request(ticket)
    {
      id: ticket.id,
      subject: ticket.subject,
      status: ticket.status,
      requester_id: ticket.requester_id,
      created_at: ticket.created_at.iso8601(3),
      updated_at: ticket.public_updated_at.iso8601(3)
    }
  end

  def serialize_ticket(ticket)
    requester = ticket.requester
    assignee = ticket.assignee
    {
      id: ticket.id,
      subject: ticket.subject,
      status: ticket.status,
      requester_id: ticket.requester_id,
      requester: {
        id: requester.id,
        name: requester.name,
        email: requester.email
      },
      assignee_id: ticket.assignee_id,
      assignee: assignee ? {
        id: assignee.id,
        name: assignee.name
      } : nil,
      created_at: ticket.created_at.iso8601(3),
      updated_at: ticket.updated_at.iso8601(3)
    }
  end

  def serialize_comment(comment)
    author = comment.author
    {
      id: comment.id,
      body: comment.body,
      public: comment.public,
      author_id: comment.author_id,
      author: {
        id: author.id,
        name: author.name
      },
      created_at: comment.created_at.iso8601(3)
    }
  end
end

  test "resend rotates token and extends expiry; revoke invalidates token and allows re-inviting" do
    inv_id = nil
    first_token = nil
    first_expires_at = nil

    travel_to Time.zone.parse("2026-11-22 10:00:00 UTC") do
      post "/api/v1/invitations",
           params: { invitation: { email: "sam@example.test", role: "agent" } },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token),
           as: :json
      assert_response :created
      inv_id = json_body.dig("invitation", "id")
      first_expires_at = Time.iso8601(json_body.dig("invitation", "expires_at"))
      _u, _a, first_token = extract_token_from_mail(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last, path: "/accept-invitation")
    end

    second_token = nil
    travel_to Time.zone.parse("2026-11-24 10:00:00 UTC") do
      assert_no_difference "Invitation.count" do
        post "/api/v1/invitations/#{inv_id}/resend", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
      end
      assert_response :ok
      assert_equal inv_id, json_body.dig("invitation", "id")
      assert_equal "pending", json_body.dig("invitation", "status")
      second_expires_at = Time.iso8601(json_body.dig("invitation", "expires_at"))
      assert second_expires_at > first_expires_at

      _u, _a, second_token = extract_token_from_mail(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last, path: "/accept-invitation")
      assert_not_equal first_token, second_token

      # First token immediately stops working on preview and acceptance
      post "/api/v1/invitation_previews",
           params: { invitation_preview: { token: first_token } },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme"),
           as: :json
      assert_response :unprocessable_content

      post "/api/v1/invitation_acceptances",
           params: { invitation_acceptance: { token: first_token, name: "Sam", password: "my-team-password" } },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme"),
           as: :json
      assert_response :unprocessable_content

      # Second token works on preview
      post "/api/v1/invitation_previews",
           params: { invitation_preview: { token: second_token } },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme"),
           as: :json
      assert_response :ok

      # Revoke invitation
      delete "/api/v1/invitations/#{inv_id}", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
      assert_response :ok
      assert_equal "revoked", json_body.dig("invitation", "status")
      assert json_body.dig("invitation", "revoked_at").present?

      # Revoked token stops working immediately
      post "/api/v1/invitation_previews",
           params: { invitation_preview: { token: second_token } },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme"),
           as: :json
      assert_response :unprocessable_content

      post "/api/v1/invitation_acceptances",
           params: { invitation_acceptance: { token: second_token, name: "Sam", password: "my-team-password" } },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme"),
           as: :json
      assert_response :unprocessable_content

      # Cannot revoke or resend an already-revoked invitation
      delete "/api/v1/invitations/#{inv_id}", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
      assert_response :unprocessable_content

      assert_no_difference -> { ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size } do
        post "/api/v1/invitations/#{inv_id}/resend", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
        assert_response :unprocessable_content
      end

      # Can re-invite the same email now that the prior invitation is revoked
      post "/api/v1/invitations",
           params: { invitation: { email: "sam@example.test", role: "agent" } },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token),
           as: :json
      assert_response :created
      assert_not_equal inv_id, json_body.dig("invitation", "id")
    end

    # Revoked invitation remains revoked even after expiry passes
    travel_to Time.zone.parse("2026-12-30 10:00:00 UTC") do
      get "/api/v1/invitations/#{inv_id}", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
      assert_response :ok
      assert_equal "revoked", json_body.dig("invitation", "status")
    end
  end

  test "tracks pending, accepted, revoked, and expired invitations with ID-asc listing and status filter" do
    ids = {}

    travel_to Time.zone.parse("2026-11-22 10:00:00 UTC") do
      # 1. Will expire
      post "/api/v1/invitations",
           params: { invitation: { email: "expired@example.test", role: "agent" } },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token),
           as: :json
      assert_response :created
      ids[:expired] = json_body.dig("invitation", "id")
      _u, _a, @expired_token = extract_token_from_mail(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last, path: "/accept-invitation")

      # 2. Will be accepted
      post "/api/v1/invitations",
           params: { invitation: { email: "accepted@example.test", role: "agent" } },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token),
           as: :json
      assert_response :created
      ids[:accepted] = json_body.dig("invitation", "id")
      _u, _a, accepted_token = extract_token_from_mail(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last, path: "/accept-invitation")

      post "/api/v1/invitation_acceptances",
           params: { invitation_acceptance: { token: accepted_token, name: "Acc", password: "accepted-password" } },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme"),
           as: :json
      assert_response :created

      # 3. Will be revoked
      post "/api/v1/invitations",
           params: { invitation: { email: "revoked@example.test", role: "admin" } },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token),
           as: :json
      assert_response :created
      ids[:revoked] = json_body.dig("invitation", "id")
      delete "/api/v1/invitations/#{ids[:revoked]}", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
      assert_response :ok
    end

    # Advance 8 days so #1 is now expired, then create #4 pending
    travel_to Time.zone.parse("2026-11-30 10:00:00 UTC") do
      post "/api/v1/invitations",
           params: { invitation: { email: "pending@example.test", role: "agent" } },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token),
           as: :json
      assert_response :created
      ids[:pending] = json_body.dig("invitation", "id")

      # Expired token rejected on preview, acceptance, resend, revoke
      post "/api/v1/invitation_previews",
           params: { invitation_preview: { token: @expired_token } },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme"),
           as: :json
      assert_response :unprocessable_content

      post "/api/v1/invitation_acceptances",
           params: { invitation_acceptance: { token: @expired_token, name: "Late", password: "late-password-1" } },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme"),
           as: :json
      assert_response :unprocessable_content

      post "/api/v1/invitations/#{ids[:expired]}/resend", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
      assert_response :unprocessable_content

      delete "/api/v1/invitations/#{ids[:expired]}", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
      assert_response :unprocessable_content

      # All 4 listed in ID ascending order
      get "/api/v1/invitations", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
      assert_response :ok
      assert_equal 4, json_body["count"]
      assert_equal [ ids[:expired], ids[:accepted], ids[:revoked], ids[:pending] ], json_body["invitations"].map { |i| i["id"] }
      assert_equal %w[expired accepted revoked pending], json_body["invitations"].map { |i| i["status"] }

      # Status filters
      %w[pending accepted revoked expired].each do |status|
        get "/api/v1/invitations?status=#{status}", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
        assert_response :ok
        assert_equal 1, json_body["count"]
        assert_equal [ ids[status.to_sym] ], json_body["invitations"].map { |i| i["id"] }
        assert_equal [ status ], json_body["invitations"].map { |i| i["status"] }
      end

      # Blank status returns all; invalid status returns 422
      get "/api/v1/invitations?status=", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
      assert_response :ok
      assert_equal 4, json_body["count"]

      get "/api/v1/invitations?status=bogus", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
      assert_response :unprocessable_content

      # Pagination works in ID ascending order
      get "/api/v1/invitations?page=1&per_page=2", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
      assert_response :ok
      assert_equal 4, json_body["count"]
      assert_equal 2, json_body["next_page"]
      assert_nil json_body["previous_page"]
      assert_equal [ ids[:expired], ids[:accepted] ], json_body["invitations"].map { |i| i["id"] }

      # Re-inviting the expired email succeeds while preserving old expired record
      post "/api/v1/invitations",
           params: { invitation: { email: "expired@example.test", role: "agent" } },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token),
           as: :json
      assert_response :created
      assert_not_equal ids[:expired], json_body.dig("invitation", "id")
    end
  end

    patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_id}",
          params: { ticket: { assignee_id: @agent_id, comment: { body: "   " } } },
          headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token),

    assert_response :unprocessable_content
    assert_nil Ticket.find(ticket_id).assignee_id

    patch "/api/v1/requests/#{ticket_id}",
          params: { request: { assignee_id: @agent_id } },
          headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token),

    assert_response :unprocessable_content
    assert_nil Ticket.find(ticket_id).assignee_id

      assert_response :created

      req_a_id = req_a_initial["id"]
    end

    travel_to Time.zone.parse("2026-11-22 10:01:00 UTC") do
      post "/api/v1/requests",
           params: { request: { subject: "Request B", comment: { body: "Second issue" } } },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token),
           as: :json
      assert_response :created
      req_b_initial = json_body["request"]
      req_b_id = req_b_initial["id"]
    end

    # Baseline order for both staff and customer: [B, A]
    get "/api/v1/requests", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token)
    assert_equal [ req_b_id, req_a_id ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }

require "test_helper"

class InvitationAndTicketIntegrityTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @acme = Account.create!(name: "Acme", subdomain: "acme")
    @globex = Account.create!(name: "Globex", subdomain: "globex")

    @acme_admin = @acme.users.create!(
      name: "Jo",
      email: "jo@acme.test",
      password: "jo-password-1",
      role: "admin",
      verified_at: Time.current
    )
    @acme_agent = @acme.users.create!(
      name: "Sam",
      email: "sam@acme.test",
      password: "sam-password-1",
      role: "agent",
      verified_at: Time.current
    )
    @acme_customer = @acme.users.create!(
      name: "Avery",
      email: "avery@example.test",
      password: "avery-password-1",
      role: "customer",
      verified_at: Time.current
    )
    @globex_admin = @globex.users.create!(
      name: "Pat",
      email: "pat@globex.test",
      password: "pat-password-1",
      role: "admin",
      verified_at: Time.current
    )
  end

  test "ticket validates assignee belongs to same account and is active staff" do
    ticket = @acme.tickets.create!(requester: @acme_customer, subject: "Help")

    ticket.assignee = @acme_customer
    assert_not ticket.valid?
    assert_includes ticket.errors[:assignee_id], "must be a staff member"

    ticket.assignee = @globex_admin
    assert_not ticket.valid?
    assert_includes ticket.errors[:assignee_id], "must belong to the same account"

    @acme_agent.update!(suspended_at: Time.current)
    ticket.assignee = @acme_agent
    assert_not ticket.valid?
    assert_includes ticket.errors[:assignee_id], "must be an active staff member"

    @acme_agent.update!(suspended_at: nil)
    ticket.assignee = @acme_agent
    assert ticket.valid?
  end

  test "private comment updates ticket updated_at without touching public_updated_at" do
    ticket = nil
    t1 = Time.zone.parse("2026-11-22 10:00:00 UTC")
    t2 = Time.zone.parse("2026-11-22 10:15:00 UTC")
    t3 = Time.zone.parse("2026-11-22 10:30:00 UTC")

    travel_to t1 do
      ticket = @acme.tickets.create!(requester: @acme_customer, subject: "Help")
      assert_equal t1, ticket.updated_at
      assert_equal t1, ticket.public_updated_at
    end

    travel_to t2 do
      ticket.comments.create!(account: @acme, author: @acme_agent, body: "Internal", public: false)
      ticket.reload
      assert_equal t2, ticket.updated_at
      assert_equal t1, ticket.public_updated_at
    end

    travel_to t3 do
      ticket.comments.create!(account: @acme, author: @acme_agent, body: "Public", public: true)
      ticket.reload
      assert_equal t3, ticket.updated_at
      assert_equal t3, ticket.public_updated_at
    end
  end

  test "invitation enforces same-account invited_by and accepted_user integrity" do
    _raw, digest = Invitation.generate_token
    inv = @acme.invitations.build(
      invited_by: @globex_admin,
      email: "new@acme.test",
      role: "agent",
      token_digest: digest,
      expires_at: 7.days.from_now
    )
    assert_not inv.valid?
    assert_includes inv.errors[:invited_by], "must belong to the same account"

    inv.invited_by = @acme_admin
    inv.accepted_user = @globex_admin
    assert_not inv.valid?
    assert_includes inv.errors[:accepted_user], "must belong to the same account"

    inv.accepted_user = nil
    assert inv.valid?
  end
end
